summary: Deep pass: No. 2 Notre Dame (6-0, 16 straight wins, all by double digits) at No. 8 BYU (5-0 SU/ATS), 5:30 PM MT, GameDay crowd. The core view stays the same, but the ranking changes: Notre Dame ML is now the anchor and most-likely-to-win leg, the BYU team-total under is the best edge, and ND -10.5 drops to a thin lean because experts are split (Covers/SI/Predictem/AtoZ on ND; VegasInsider/ATS.io on BYU) and Freeman is only 2-4 in true road games. BYU's offense without RB LJ Martin (out 4-6 wks) scored 24 vs Iowa State and 17 at TCU, and now faces the FBS No. 1 total defense (214 ypg, 11.0 ppg). Correction to the first pass: the 2022 meeting was ND 28-20, not 20-16.

legs.note: Most likely to win. ND has won 16 straight, all by double digits, and preseason SP+ had a large gap (ND 3rd at +25.8 with the No. 3 O and No. 9 D; BYU 18th at +15.5). Preseason ESPN FPI made ND 76% here. BYU is down its Big 12 OPOY RB. The risks are Freeman's 2-4 record in true road games, ND not having won at a top-10 team since 2012, and the night crowd. Priced near fair (0.778), so this is a safety leg, not value.

Best edge. ND allows 11.0 ppg (4th) and 214 ypg (1st), with 15 sacks, 7 INTs and an FBS-high 5 forced fumbles. Without Martin, BYU's run game is a committee (Rex/Tonga) plus Bachmeier's legs. The offense scored 17 at TCU and 24 vs Iowa State (329 pass / 109 rush from Bachmeier). Bachmeier's career line is solid but not elite: 64.9%, 7.8 YPA, 15/7 TD/INT in 2025. Against that, BYU is at home and a single short field or special-teams score changes the math. Market fair is 0.534.

Only 2 of BYU's 5 games went over, and its last two finished 17-10 and 24-10. The under is 3-0 in the last 3 meetings (2022: 28-20), and the total has dropped from 48.5 to 46.5. ND, though, has gone over in 4 of 6 and scored 58 last week, so its explosiveness is the risk. Most of the edge is gone at 46.5.

ND's 16-game double-digit streak and the Martin injury support the cover, as do Covers (Powers, ND by 13), SI, Predictem and AtoZ (30-15). Against it: BYU is 5-0 ATS, VegasInsider and ATS.io take BYU +10.5, public tickets are on BYU, and ND's road résumé under Freeman is weak. This is close to a coin flip, so keep it a lean.

research:
1. QBs/personnel: ND QB CJ Carr. In 2025 he went 66.6%, 9.4 YPA, 168.1 rating. In 2026 he was 88/124 (71%), 1,197 yds, 13 TD, 1 INT through 5 games (StatSniper), with 14/22, 237, 3 TD vs Purdue (FLM). PFF had 0 INT on 76 dropbacks as of 9/24. Backup: Kenny Minchey left for Kentucky, so the likely QB2 is RS-Fr Blake Hebert (unproven); ND named no official QB2 (Matt Fortuna/AtoZ). ND RB Jonaz Walton (Fr) had 181 yds vs Stanford, including a 97-yd TD (AP). BYU QB Bear Bachmeier, career at BYU only: 2025 251/387 (64.9%), 3,033 yds, 7.8 YPA, 15 TD/7 INT, plus 527 rush yds and 11 TD (ESPN/cfbstats). In 2026 he was ~70% early with a 188.2 rating (Deseret), then 22/30, 329 yds, 2 TD and 109 rush yds vs ISU (AP). I found no data on BYU's QB2.
2. Injuries: BYU RB LJ Martin (2025 Big 12 OPOY) is OUT 4-6 wks with a lower-leg injury (Thamel/Deseret). Sitake says he will be week-to-week soon. OL Andrew Gentry is out (ankle surgery), and every other player has a chance to play (Deseret 10/14). Replacements are Preston Rex and Fr Journee Tonga by committee. ND CB Leonard Moore (concussion) is questionable but practiced, and ND is preparing as if he plays (Rotoballer 10/15). DT Jason Onye (ankle) is questionable. LB Viliamu-Asa is off the report (FLM). I found no final game-day report.
3. Advanced: Preseason SP+ had ND 3rd (+25.8; O 3rd 40.2, D 9th 14.6, ST 47th) and BYU 18th (+15.5; O 16th, D 20th, ST 45th) (Eleven Warriors/Deseret). Preseason FPI made ND 76%, and this was BYU's only game as an underdog (SI/SDS). ND: 44.0 ppg, 456.7 ypg, allows 214 ypg (1st) and 11.0 ppg (4th), with 15 sacks, 7 INT and 5 FF (FBS-best) (ABC7/Fox). BYU: 34.6 ppg, allows 254.4 ypg (8th) and 13.4 ppg. Akana has 3.5 sacks and 6.5 TFL. SI ranks BYU only 29th in opponent success rate and calls its run D a weakness vs ND's run game. Live 2026 SP+/EPA was not found.
4. Scheme: ND is balanced (262 pass / 195 rush ypg) with explosive Walton runs, facing a BYU front that allowed ISU only 200 total yds. BYU's run-first attack (224 rush ypg) now relies on Bachmeier's legs plus a committee, facing ND's No. 3 run D and a disruptive front (Traore 3.5 sacks). Carr's accuracy (71%, 1 INT) faces a BYU pass D allowing 174 ypg.
5. Coaching: Freeman is 43-12 overall and 24-4 over the last two years, but 2-4 in true road games, and ND hasn't beaten a top-10 team on the road since 2012 (Roundtable 10/12). Sitake has gone 23-4 over two seasons, and BYU is 24-16 ATS as an underdog since 2016 (60%, TheSpread, dated). I found no 4th-down or post-bye splits.
6. Situational: this is the first top-10 game ever in Provo, with GameDay there for the first time since 2009, a 5:30 PM MT ABC night game, ~4,550 ft altitude, and some of the priciest tickets of the weekend (KSL). BYU played Friday 10/9 and gets 8 days of rest. ND played Sat 10/10 at home. It is the first game of a home-and-home (AP).
7. History: ND leads the series 7-2. The last meeting was 2022 in Las Vegas, ND 28-20 (AP; the first pass wrongly said 20-16). The under is 3-0 in the last 3 meetings and ND is 2-1 ATS (SI). BYU is 5-0 ATS in 2026 and ND is 4-2 ATS. Overs: ND 4/6, BYU 2/5 (SI).
8. Weather: sunny, low 60s at kickoff, cooling after dark, no wind or precipitation concern (KSL/East Idaho News).
9. Experts and market: Brad Powers (Covers) ND -9.5/-10.5, rates ND by 13. SI (Iain) ND -10.5. Predictem ND covers. AtoZ (Rob Gregson) ND 30-15 (under 46.5 and BYU TT under). VegasInsider BYU +10.5. ATS.io leans BYU. numberFire 56.5% (ND side). Consensus leans ND ATS, about 4 named sources to 2. I found no strong named pick on the total. Line: ND opened -11.5, went to -9.5, now -10.5 (-11 at BetMGM). Total moved 48.5 -> 46.5, and Kalshi has the over at 47%. BettingPros says public tickets favor BYU +10. Searches hit the tool budget at 22, so no live splits.
